newsitem.title: UK: China move may send Hong Kong negative signal - UK.
newsitem.headline: China move may send Hong Kong negative signal - UK.

text.p: China's decision to send 4,000 troops into Hong Kong on July 1, just hours after the transfer of sovereignty from Britain, may send a "negative signal" to Hong Kong people and the world, Britain said on Friday.

A Foreign Office spokesman said: We recognise that the defence of Hong Kong after June 30 is a matter for the Chinese authorities, but we are concerned that the manner of the...deployment may send a negative signal to the people of Hong Kong and the international community."
The spokesman, replying to a question, said Britain had consistently urged the Chinese to handle the deployment of the garrison "with the greatest possible sensiivity".

The office of Hong Kong's chief executive-designate, Tung Chee-hwa, said earlier that the troops, backed by helicopters, ships and armoured vehicles, would arrive in Hong Kong six hours after Britain returns it to China.
Britain's last governor of its only remaining large colony, Chris Patten, said the move was "a most appalling signal to send to the people of Hong Kong".

British Prime Minister Tony Blair will fly out to Hong Kong on Sunday to be present at the handover ceremony. His office said he was expected to have talks with Patten and his deputy Anson Chan, Chief Secretary and head of the civil service.
